reason: A: the yellow #FLATTENTHECURVE bar stops halfway across the top, so it looks cut off. The headline is small and leaves a large empty block in the bottom-left. The symptom list starts right at the top edge, and the yellow CTA is crammed under the list with almost no gap. B: the headline is large and dominant, and the hashtag sits in a deliberate yellow box. However, 'SYMPTOMS' nearly touches the symptom list, which now wraps badly ('breath Dry / cough') and runs from the top edge to the bottom edge. The doctor is shrunk into a small right-hand vignette with the CTA tucked tight under it. B has the better hierarchy and use of space.

A: the headline is shrunk to a small block. Its first line sits on the bottom edge of the T's crossbar, half on red and half on blue, which breaks the original's text-in-bar relationship. The tiny type leaves huge dead blue areas, so the copy no longer leads. B: it keeps the original structure: the first two lines sit inside the red crossbar, the rest runs down over the stem, and the type is large and legible. But everything is crammed into the left 65%, leaving the right third empty and lopsided. Lines like 'AGAINST CRUELTY' still straddle the red/blue edge, as they do in the original.

A leaves the peach panel and pattern ending around y≈380, so there is a dead white strip across the bottom. The whole composition sits high, and the www.cascadia.us URL is jammed onto the frame's bottom ornament, where it collides with the border. B extends the panel and photos to fill the height and keeps the framed logo block centred with the URL inside the frame. Its only flaw is a thin white strip under the peach panel at the bottom edge, which needs minor polish.

A keeps the quote's original three-line wrap and puts it beside a crowd image that bleeds off the top-left, which reads as a proper banner. But the quote is small for this height, the rightmost figure nearly touches the text column, and the image's bottom edge fades out unevenly. B re-wraps the quote badly: 'THOUGHTFUL' and 'WORLD; INDEED,' are left as orphan lines, which makes a ragged five-line block. Its crowd image also floats in an arbitrary inset box with figures sliced at the left edge, and the attribution is jammed tight under the quote.

A: the 'PODCAST WITH HARRY LEE HOFFMAN' subtitle sits about 80 px below the headline, so the title block reads as two separate pieces. The subtitle is also very small, and there is a dead band between them. B: headline and subtitle stay tightly grouped as in the original, but the arrow doodle now lands on the man's hair, an unintended collision, and the top of the canvas is left fairly empty. B's text grouping is closer to the original, so it edges ahead.

A: the illustration is jammed against the left canvas edge, the quote block floats left of centre and leaves a large dead area on the right, and the quote is fairly small for the format. B: the quote is larger and better centred in the right column, and the illustration has a proper margin, but the attribution sits cramped right under 'MAKEUP.' close to the bottom edge. In both, the frame shows a stock 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION / HAND DRAWN ELEMENTS' label instead of the quote-in-frame concept, and that label is tiny and unreadable.

A shrinks the whole composition into the top ~70% and shifts it left, leaving a dead white band across the bottom third with a stray hairline at y≈548. The quote's lines 'JEALOUS BECAUSE' and 'THEY CAN'T WEAR' also run into the frame's inner rule. That is a shrink, not a resize. B scales the illustrated frame to fill the width and keeps the quote centred, so it stays faithful to the original. But the same quote lines still touch the inner border, the right-side orchid and flowers nearly hit the canvas edge, and there is an uneven empty strip below the art (more space at the bottom than at the top) with a faint hairline at y≈672.

A is just the original pillarboxed: there are white empty bars down both sides because the green background and forest were not extended. That makes it an unadapted, unshippable copy, though the text, dividers and hierarchy are intact. B has the same white bars, and it also moves the cream divider up into the treeline as a stray line, drops the second divider, and pushes 'March 21' into the trees. Its headline runs to the canvas edges with no margin, so B is worse.

A breaks the design: the headline 'Order online' has shrunk to a tiny block off-axis from the rules, while 'food & drinks' is blown up larger than the headline and runs onto the kraft box. That inverts the hierarchy and leaves the rules floating apart from the text. B keeps the original's centred lockup (rules, headline, subline) intact and in proportion on a nearly identical canvas; it only needs minor polish, since the left side has a little more empty space and the bottom box sits close to the edge.

A keeps the original's structure: big letterform graphics on the left, headline on white at the right. But there is a visible seam under the top ART row, with clipped coloured slivers and a pink line, the last ART is cropped to 'AR', and the bottom letterforms are cut off hard. B lays a white panel over the left-side letterform graphics, so the key 'RT'/'n' artwork shrinks to cut-off fragments at the left edge and bottom. The headline then sits on the left with a large empty white area to its right: a big loss of fidelity and badly balanced.

A keeps the original layout, with the big lettering on the left and the quote on clean white space at the right. But the top row of ART words is sliced off at the canvas edge so the brand wordmarks don't read, and a new magenta 'T' block crowds the quote on the right. B moves the quote to the far left, jammed against beige and purple fragments, and leaves a large empty white band in the middle. Its lettering is cropped to unreadable bits along the top and bottom edges, so the original's bold letterform imagery is lost.

A just drops the whole banner into the middle of the square at its original size, leaving about 60% of the canvas as empty white bands above and below. The text is small and there's no rearrangement, but the composition, brand and graphics are intact and the text stays readable. B breaks 'HOHOHO AGENCY' into two lines with very different sizes, crams the decorations into a tiny strip that collides with 'HOHOHO', and scatters crescent and triangle fragments clipped at hard edges. Its layout has no grid, balance or recognisable link to the original, so it's unusable.

A: the two text blocks sit side by side at different sizes and baselines, the divider line is stranded under 'Rough' and separates nothing, and the rose is cut off along a hard vertical edge on its right; the rose still reads as the central hero, though. B: the text drifts down the canvas in a staggered, misaligned cascade, and the divider is pushed beside 'Great' instead of between the two blocks. The cropped rose is jammed into the bottom-left corner, leaving the whole bottom-right quarter empty, so the layout is badly lopsided.

A keeps the brick as a large hero and the price is prominent, but the brick is cut off by a hard vertical edge at the X shape, 'Sets for kids' sits jammed against the headline and the brick's top, and the columns are crowded. B shrinks the brick and X to a tiny icon and shrinks $14.99 to near-caption size, which kills the hierarchy. It also sets the headline as 'CONS TRUC / TION' on one wide line, which reads as a typo, and leaves dead space between the headline and the scattered right-hand cluster.

The two are almost the same and share the same faults. The headline still reads 'CONS TRUC TION', so the word stays broken in a banner that has room for it on one line. 'ORDER NOW' is tiny and too thin to read. The price sits after the button, which breaks the reading order. The X graphic and brick are crammed against 'Buy 2 only for', and the text sits on the graphic. A's brick is smaller and gets lost under the text. B's brick is slightly larger and reads better as the product, but it is just as cramped.

A keeps the yellow LOVE. CARE. KIDS. block and the mother-and-baby photo, but the photo is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed against the right edge. A wide empty white gap separates it from the headline, so the banner reads as two scattered fragments, and the thin yellow frame is gone. B centres the headline block but shrinks the key photo to an unrecognisable sliver at the far left and adds a stray yellow fragment in the top-right corner, so the core imagery is lost and the layout reads as broken.

Neither candidate bleeds the building photo to the left edge the way the original does. In both, it floats at x≈175 with a dead white strip to its left, which breaks the original composition. A keeps the headline larger and anchored to the right margin, so it is the clear focal point. B shrinks the headline further and pulls it inward, leaving lopsided empty space on the right and making the message weaker at banner size.

Both just drop the original strip into the middle of the taller canvas. The tooth shapes are sliced flat at about y=148, and there are dead blue bands above and below, so it looks like a cropped, pasted banner rather than a re-arranged one. A is worse because it also shrinks the 'DENTAL SERVICES' headline to a small, weak label that no longer dominates. B keeps the headline at a size that leads the layout, although 'SERVICES' butts against the big tooth's edge.

A: the black/orange/green ART wordmarks at the top are sliced through, so they read as garbled fragments. The left graphic cluster is broken into disconnected strips along the bottom. The headline is shrunk, pushed left and crowded against the beige shape with no clear grid. B: it keeps the original structure better, with the big graphic on the left and the headline larger on the right, but the top ART row is still cropped to half-letters. A stray magenta T block crowds the right edge next to the headline, and the bottom shapes are cut off.

Both carry over the vertical line breaks as 'CONS TRUC TION', which reads as three broken words on one line. Both cram the brick, 'Buy 2 only for', a tiny ORDER NOW button and the $14.99 price into the right third, so the price comes after the CTA and is too small to stand out. A's larger brick butts right up against 'Buy 2'. B's slightly smaller brick leaves a hair more clearance, but otherwise the two are almost identical.

A: the hero photo is reduced to an unrecognisable scrap at far left, a stray yellow sliver clips the top-right edge, and the centred yellow headline block floats in empty white with no image. The original's key visual is effectively gone. B: keeps the headline block and a small but recognisable mother-and-baby photo on the right, which reads left to right. Still, the photo is a tiny thumbnail, most of the strip is dead white, the yellow frame motif is gone and the headline is small. It is weak but more faithful than A.

A does turn the design into a left-to-right banner, but the hierarchy is inverted: the headline 'JOIN OUR CHOIR!' is shrunk to tiny type while the secondary line 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!' is the biggest element. The white cloud graphic sits detached on the white background, so it reads as stray outline debris rather than the brand shape. B is just the original shrunk into the middle of the banner, with huge dead areas on both sides, and 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!' is so small it can't be read, so B fails the fit-to-format and readability criteria outright.

Both leave the geometric background unscaled: it stops about 60px short of the square canvas, so blank white bands run across the top and bottom. In A, the white frame is shoved up and out of register. Its top edge sits above where the background starts, its bottom edge cuts across the pink band well above the background's end, and the text card sits high and off-centre inside it. B keeps the frame and card centred and in proportion with the original's composition and type hierarchy, so it is the less broken resize. Its empty top and bottom bands are still a fail that must be fixed before shipping.

A is a shrunken copy of the square design dropped left of centre. Large empty blue areas sit on both sides, and the T stem stops just short of the bottom edge instead of bleeding off it, so the banner shape goes unused, but the headline's line breaks and the text-to-T relationship survive. B has the same small, centred, dead-space problem and is worse: 'NOW!' is orphaned on its own line, which breaks the headline's first line apart, and 'TO ANIMALS' straddles the red/blue stem edge more awkwardly.

A keeps the photos and the headline frame, but the top half is a squashed copy of the original. The bottom half is mostly dead white space, and the plate sketch, Cascadia, RESTAURANT and the URL fall outside the frame in a loose column down the left edge. The tall frame is also mostly empty under the headline. B is unusable: both food photos have shrunk to tiny thumbnails inside the pattern tiles. The frame, plate sketch and divider ornaments are scattered as random fragments across the canvas, and the oversized divider beside the headline looks like a mistake, with no hierarchy or grouping anywhere.

A keeps the overlay panel running off the bottom edge and keeps the X/slash/circle marks at the panel's corners like the original, with a clean centred text stack. Its flaws: the marks are tight against the panel edges and half-cross them, the top of the canvas feels cramped, and the type sits smaller in a shrunken frame. B cuts the panel off at about 255 px, which leaves a stray strip of photo under it and makes it look unfinished. B's corner marks float well outside the narrower panel over busy hands, so they no longer frame anything. Its headline and the 'Join WADE team' line are also smaller and weaker than A's.

A: the headline is big and readable, but the windmill icon is shrunk to a tiny speck squeezed into a jumbled strip of shapes on the left, and those shapes are crushed miniatures of the original. The text breaks into four lines ('ENERGY FOR / FUTURE / SUMMIT / MARCH 18') and the date has no visual separation from the title. The two diagonal lines are stranded on the right, so the layout is lopsided and fails as a fit to the format. B: it is just the original shrunk into a centred box with large empty margins on both sides. The headline is tiny and barely readable, and the background shapes are cut off at the box edges. It keeps fidelity but fails readability and does not suit the banner shape. A is less bad because its message is readable.

Both crop the photo so the eyes and top of the face are cut off, which loses the 'looking up' idea, and the doodles are scattered without purpose. A is worse: the lightbulb doodle sits right on the mouth and teeth, and the question-mark doodle is jammed against the headline's '?'. B's lightbulb still overlaps the edge of the cheek, but its question mark sits clear to the left of the headline and the text block has more room.

A: the frame grid is cut off from the text and sits empty at the left edge, and the play icon floats on its own. Reading order is jumbled: tickets comes before 'Theatre presents' and the credit line. The copy is tiny and crammed into the orange strip, and the photo is a blurry, darkened crop that loses the warm orange tone. B is worse: the frame's lines run straight through the text (strike-throughs on 'Theatre presents' and 'High school office'), and 'Pygmalion', the credit and the tickets text spill past the orange strip onto the busy photo. The play icon is jammed against the headline, so the whole thing reads as collisions everywhere.

A enlarges the controller icons and jams the headline right under them with almost no gap, which leaves a dead band at the top and an empty bottom. Its left edges are also ragged: the headline starts at x≈63, the body copy at ≈70 and the URL is centred, so the original's clean left axis is gone. B keeps the original's structure: icons centred with generous space before the headline, and every text block on one shared left edge with the original's size steps. Its only flaws are slightly wide side margins and small fine print, which are minor polish.

A: the forest background covers only a narrow centre strip, with white space on both sides. The headline, subline and body copy run past it onto the white, so they are clipped at both edges ('cial Event Dev…', 'International I…'), the white text vanishes, and a divider line floats off to the right. B has the same white-margin failure: the headline is clipped ('Special Event', 'nternational'), 'Joint celebration & Forest cleanup' is split into a jammed fragment at the lower left, the body copy runs off the right edge, and 'March 21' is almost invisible at the top left. Both are unusable. A is marginally less bad because its reading order and stacking stay closer to the original.

A is the original copied unchanged onto the square canvas: a wide white dead zone sits on the left and a blank strip on the right, and nothing was rearranged for the new format, but the stripes, card and type are all intact. B breaks the design apart: white gaps split the stripes, the blue and red stripes are notched at the top, and every stripe stops at about 88% height, leaving an empty band at the bottom. B's white card also ends abruptly, with TRAVEL MUGS jammed against its bottom edge, so it reads as a broken layout rather than a resize.

A rearranges the design properly for a banner: a large headline on the left, the cat group on the right, and good contrast. Its flaws are small: the cat illustration ends in a flat cut about 20px above the bottom edge instead of bleeding off it like the original, and 'AND' sits alone on its own line. B is just a shrunk copy of the original centred on the canvas: the headline is tiny and no longer the focal point, the cats are small, and large empty purple areas on both sides make it look unfinished.

A and B are pixel-for-pixel almost the same as the original. Both keep the headline / stained-glass window / details banner layout with brand colours and font intact. They share the same minor flaws: 'Sunday' sits only a few pixels from the window's left edge, the grey date and address text is small and low-contrast, and the band of white space below the content is unbalanced. I see no difference between them that matters.

A keeps the stained-glass window clear of the edges with even top and bottom margins and keeps the original's three-column structure. But it shrank everything: the date and address text is tiny and hard to read, and the three groups float far apart with large empty gutters. B has a larger, more readable headline and details, but the window runs almost edge to edge, jammed against the top and bottom of the canvas so it looks cropped. That breaks the original's breathing room and makes the centre feel cramped next to wide empty sides.

A keeps the owls at their original size, so the extra height reads as padding. Worse, the right owl's flat-cut body stops short of the bottom edge and leaves a white strip under it, so it looks clipped and floating. B scales the owls and the headline up to fill the taller canvas and keeps the right owl anchored to the bottom edge, so it looks deliberate. Its only small flaws are the purple star crowding the 'P' of PARTIES and the left owl's head cropping hard at the top.

A keeps the brick-and-X hero at a strong size and reads in a sensible left-to-right order: headline, product, offer, price, CTA. It has clear flaws, though. 'Sets for kids' is jammed right up against the stacked 'CONS/TRUC/TION' headline, and 'Buy 2 only for' almost touches the X. The left margin is a dead area, and the headline is still split into word fragments. B is worse. It sets the headline on one line as 'CONS TRUC TION' with spaces, which reads as broken words. The key product image shrinks to a tiny icon jammed into the top-right corner. The price comes after the ORDER NOW button and is squeezed against the right edge, which breaks the reading order, and the right half is a scattered cluster with uneven spacing.

A is unusable: the headline, the URL and the 'HO SMART' wordmark are gone, and the logo icon is pale grey on white with nothing next to it. The blue band is cut off at the top, and the photo is cropped and floats with its diagonal lines misplaced and large dead areas around it. B keeps the brand, copy and imagery intact and readable, but it is just the original banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle of a square canvas, leaving about 85% of it empty white. That fails 'rearrange, don't shrink', but it is the less bad of the two.

A is unusable: the headline, URL and 'HO SMART' wordmark have vanished (white text left on white). The logo icon floats as a faint grey outline, the blue panel is a cropped wedge, and the bottom ~60% of the canvas is empty. B keeps the whole design intact and readable but just shrinks the banner into a thin strip in the middle of a blank portrait canvas, so the text is small, about 85% of the space is dead and nothing was rearranged for the tall format. It is still clearly broken, just less so than A.

A is the banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle of the square. About 75% of the canvas above and below it is empty navy, 'Baby Toddler' is tiny and the dot clusters sit cramped against the edges, so nothing was rearranged for the new shape. B does restack the design, with the image band on top and a larger logo and 'BEDDING' lockup below. But the top-left dot grid sits over the image band, the side dot clusters float with no connection to anything, and the bottom ~55% of the canvas is dead space, so the layout is badly top-heavy. B is still the less bad of the two.

A breaks up the 'Baby & Toddler BEDDING' title: the ampersand and 'Baby/Toddler' sit in the middle of the banner with a wide dead gap before BEDDING, so the name no longer reads as one unit. The '&' is also clipped at the bottom, and the left dot grids are jammed against the edge. B keeps the original title together and keeps the photo strip running behind the '&'. Its flaws: the photo strip starts late, leaving a dead band on the left; BEDDING is smaller than in the original, leaving empty space to its right; and the tiny 'Baby/Toddler' text crowds into BEDDING.

A: the illustration clusters have shrunk to tiny thumbnails pushed against the left and right edges, and 'CREATIVE AGENCY' sits about 200 px below 'CLAYTONI', leaving large dead navy areas, so the title and its tagline no longer read as one lockup. B is worse: 'CLAYTONI' is jammed against the top edge, the tagline is pushed to the bottom edge, and a vast empty middle holds only the same tiny edge-hugging illustrations, so the layout is split apart with no visual centre.

A: the frame's rules cut straight through 'THEATRE PRESENTS' and 'HIGH SCHOOL OFFICE', the text spills past the orange strip onto the dark photo, the headline and arrow overlap the frame edge, and the orange tint over the photo is gone. B has no collisions and the text stays inside the strip, but the order is jumbled (tickets line above 'Richmond High School Theatre presents'), all the secondary text is tiny, and the frame and arrow sit empty and cut off at the left and bottom edges, away from the content.

A is the original banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle of the square. Everything stays readable and on brand, but about 85% of the canvas is dead white space, so it fits the format badly and nothing has been rearranged. B is unusable: the headline, the URL and the 'HO SMART' wordmark are gone (probably white text on a white background), and the logo outline floats almost invisible on white. On top of that, the blue panel is an empty chopped shape, the diagonal stripes cut across the hand photo, and the photo sits in an arbitrary inset with no alignment to anything else.

A keeps GET A GIFT as the dominant headline, but 'GIFT' runs onto the photo edge, and 'with your next cup of coffee' and 'Only this Christmas' sit in white over the busy sweater and mug photo. The stars land on the red box, the divider lines cut across, and the URL is stranded under the gift icons. B gets the hierarchy backwards: the secondary 'with your next cup of coffee' is huge and sits on the busy photo, while GET A GIFT shrinks to a minor label under oversized gift icons. The stars collide with 'Only this Christmas', the URL is tiny, and stray dashed lines fill the bottom-left.

A extends the orange header and the photo to fill most of the square and keeps the text intact, but it leaves an odd thin white strip above the orange band (~20px) and a thicker unbalanced white strip at the bottom, so it looks like a fill error. B is just the original letterboxed: the same layout sits unchanged between ~60px white bars at top and bottom, so nothing was rearranged for the square and the top bar reads as dead space.

Both drop the praying-hands photo, the sparkles and the cloud shape, leaving bare black text on white with a stray speck at the far right, so the design is no longer recognisable. A also shrinks 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!' to an unreadable smudge, with a weak headline floating in dead space on the left. B's headline is larger and its subline is barely legible, but it is still a generic centred text strip with no brand imagery.

A is a real vertical reflow (hashtag pill, stacked headline, list, doctor, CTA), but the narrow column merges the symptom list into misleading lines like 'Shortness of breath Dry cough' and 'Sore throat Headache'. The yellow CTA is also jammed against the bottom edge under the illustration, and the hashtag bar is shrunk to a small pill. B is the square layout scaled down into a middle band, with large dead purple areas above and below. Its list and CTA are tiny and hard to read, and the doctor is cut off flat at the band's bottom edge, so it reads as a shrunk copy, not a resize.

A breaks the design apart. 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' and 'THE MINIMALIST' are pulled to the far left, away from the headline. 'DEAN COOPER' runs over the cut-off pattern strip and its white card edge. The frame and the two pink dots end up in an empty box on the right, so most of the banner is dead white space. B keeps the text block together and in the right order, but the pattern is cut down to thin slivers at the top and bottom of a narrow centre column. The empty frame with its dots sits alone on the left, the right third is blank, and the layout is a shrunken square in a banner instead of being rearranged to read left to right.

Both pull the headline off the red T, so the original's signature layered lockup is lost and the T becomes a separate block with no link to the text. Both also break the headline into an awkwardly ragged stack ('JOIN / VOLUNTEERING / NOW!'). A puts the text and the T together in the top two-thirds and leaves about a third of the canvas empty at the bottom. B spreads the elements over the full height, so it balances slightly better, but it leaves a wide dead gap between the headline and the T.

A is a plain crop that shrinks the title block: 'Spa Utopia' is tiny and lost in the middle of the banner, and the 'Weekly SPA items review' tagline is too small to read. It keeps the original's quiet composition and the brush stroke behind the title. B makes the title huge and puts it on one line, but it runs straight over the green bottle, dropper and glass jar. The tagline is too big, wraps to two lines and sits on the busy leaves. The brush stroke now floats on its own with no text on it, so B has more collisions and loses more of the original's look.

A is just the original shrunk into the left half: the right ~45% of the banner is empty grey, the text is small, and the layout is badly lopsided. Still, the red panel, quote, attribution and skyline keep their original relationships. B fills the canvas but breaks the design: a decorative line cuts through 'MODERN' in the headline, the bottom half of the red panel is empty, the attribution floats off to the side, and the skyline becomes a small separate thumbnail in a white box, so the signature skyline-over-panel image is lost.

A shoves the whole composition to the left. The skyline ends abruptly at about x=580 and leaves a dead grey band with a visible background seam on the right, so it looks lopsided and unfinished. B keeps the card, quote and attribution centred and in proportion, but it is still a shrunken copy: the skyline stops short of both canvas edges, the grey side margins have hard seams, and the city base no longer runs full-bleed the way it does in the original.

A: the wind-turbine icon, the original's focal image, has shrunk to an unrecognisable cyan blob that looks clipped at the top-left, so the key imagery is effectively lost. The corner shapes are reduced to meaningless slivers and the two-line headline is just the original block shrunk and centred, not rearranged for a banner. B: the turbine is still recognisable, but it is tiny and jammed against the 'E' of the headline with no gutter. The headline still stacks on two lines, crowding the 50 px height, and the green, blue and red shapes are scattered fragments, though B keeps more of the brand imagery than A.

A is the original landscape shrunk into a thin band across the middle of the portrait canvas. About 60% of the canvas is dead yellow above and below, and the headline and the SALE discs are small, but everything stays intact, aligned and readable. B is broken: the S, A and L letters are tiny and float off-centre inside oversized discs, the SALE stack is pushed to the right edge, the headline is shrunk to a small corner label, and the decorations are scattered and duplicated with no hierarchy.

A: the photo is cropped to just the mouth and cheek, so the person reads as a meaningless fragment. The headline is small and squeezed into a stacked block with tiny subtitle text, and the bulb and question-mark doodles crowd against it while the right two-thirds of the banner is almost empty. B: it has the same mouth-only crop, and the bulb, question-mark and atom doodles are piled directly on the face, an unintended-looking collision. Still, its headline is much larger and reads clearly left to right, with the subtitle and molecule spread across the width, so its hierarchy and fit to the banner shape are better.

A pulls the quote out of the frame, which uncovers a stock placeholder ('BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION / HAND DRAWN ELEMENTS') inside the shrunken frame. The quote sits loose below it, and the attribution floats off to the right with no shared alignment, so the framed-quote concept is lost and the brand looks broken. B keeps the original intact and recognisable, but it is basically the original scaled onto the square with empty margins on the left and right. The 'JEALOUS BECAUSE' and 'THEY CAN'T WEAR' lines still run into the inner frame border, a flaw carried over from the original that should have been fixed.

A keeps more of the city imagery, but the diamond collage has broken down into a hard-edged rectangular photo block with stray white diamond fragments. The 'Fenix Ave' diamond sits on top of this mess, and the date diamond floats alone at the far right. There is dead white space above the headline, and the divider line has dropped to the bottom-right corner, cut off from the headline. B is worse: the collage is gone, leaving a small stamp-sized photo and an empty white lattice of diamond outlines on the right, an obvious leftover. The body copy is tiny and set apart from the headline, the three diamond/photo blocks are spread evenly across the top with no hierarchy, and the divider line floats with no purpose. B's two-line headline is stronger, but the brand imagery is mostly lost.

A: the invite copy runs right up to the left canvas edge. The cross floats in the gap between the invite copy and 'Worship & Bible Study', which is stranded beside the illustration, and the dates are small and cut off below. Reading order is jumbled. B: the left-headline / middle-copy / right-image structure reads well from left to right, but the cross is blown up into a huge, blurry blob that overpowers the copy. The dates line is jammed under the invite text and crowds 'ANTHONY'.

Both banners have the same faults: the invite line and the dates are too small to read at this height, and a small decorative cross has been blown up into a blurry focal point that pulls attention from the headline. In A the cross stays inside the frame and 'Worship & Bible Study' sits under it as in the original, though that line nearly touches the bottom edge. In B the cross runs the full banner height and is cut off at the top and bottom, which makes it even more dominant and pixelated, so B is slightly worse.

A: the invite copy sits left of the headline, so supporting text is read before 'YOUTH CAMP'. The illustration is squeezed between the headline and the dates, the dates are jammed against the right edge with 'AUGUST 4-20' badly broken, and all secondary text is too small to read. B: the dates lead on the far left with the same awkward wrapping, and the cross is crammed against the illustration's edge. Its flow (image, then headline, then the worship line, then the invite) is slightly more logical, but the type is just as tiny and the layout just as cramped.

A keeps the original structure: the hanging owl at the top, the centered 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow, then the headline, then the blue owl at the bottom. Its flaws are confetti squeezed into one band that runs behind the headline letters, the bottom owl cropped hard at the edge, and empty gaps around the text block. B has the wrong reading order, with the eyebrow placed below the headline and left-aligned while the headline is centered. The hanging owl floats in the middle, cut off flat at the top, and the blue owl is shrunk to a tiny corner icon, so the pair of owls no longer balances and there is a large empty area below.

A breaks the design into three unrelated pieces spread across the banner: the yellow headline card on the left, an empty outlined frame in the middle that holds nothing, and the photo on the right. A yellow accent stub also floats in the top-right corner, and the headline no longer sits on the photo, so the layering is lost; but the headline is readable and the layout does read left to right. B just shrinks the whole original and centres it, leaving about 75% of the canvas as dead white on both sides, and 'LOVE. CARE. KIDS.' becomes tiny, barely legible text, which is exactly the shrink-not-rearrange failure the brief warns against.

A shrinks the hero photo to an unreadable ~12px thumbnail stranded left of centre, leaves the yellow headline block floating in the middle with tiny text, and has a stray yellow sliver clipped at the top-right edge. Most of the banner is dead white, and the outline frame and the photo's role as the key image are gone. B is still weak: the headline block on the left and the small photo on the right sit at opposite ends of a vast empty middle, the photo is too small to carry the design, and the same yellow fragment is cut off at the top-right. Even so, B's headline is legible, the photo can be recognised, and the banner reads left to right.

The two are almost identical. Both shrink the original into a 320x50 strip, and the side illustrations are cropped and jammed against the left and right edges, so the figures read as clutter rather than characters. In A the 'CREATIVE AGENCY' subtitle is slightly larger and easier to read; in B it is noticeably tinier at this size, though the CLAYTONI headline, colours and balance are kept in both.

Both lose the original's main idea: the headline no longer sits layered on the red T. Instead the T is a separate shape parked below the text, so it reads as an unrelated block. A keeps the original line break 'AGAINST CRUELTY' and spreads its weight more evenly, but leaves a big ~135px gap between the text and the T and empty space at the top. B breaks the line awkwardly into 'AGAINST / CRUELTY', and its T stops about two-thirds of the way down, leaving roughly 190px of dead blue space at the bottom, so the layout is lopsided and top-heavy.

A breaks the main message. The SALE letters are tiny and sit at the bottom edges of oversized, mostly empty circles that are jammed against the right edge of the canvas. 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' has shrunk to a small, off-centre label at the top-left. The lanterns, clouds and ingots are duplicated and scattered, so there is no clear focal point. B is the original shrunk into a band across the middle, with about 35% of the canvas left as empty yellow above and below. That is a letterbox, not a rearrangement for the story format, and the headline and SALE are small for the format. Still, B keeps the hierarchy, symmetry and legible lettering intact, so it is the less bad of the two.

A: the headline 'HOW IT WORKS?' is large and clearly the focal point, but the photo is cropped to a disembodied mouth and ear. The bulb, question-mark and atom doodles are piled onto the face, which looks cluttered and unintentional, and the 'PODCAST WITH' line is tiny. B: the headline is shrunk very small and jammed into a narrow centre stack with illegible subtitle text, the doodles are tiny scraps, and the crop is again just a smile, with a large dead area to the right. B has weaker hierarchy and is harder to read than A.

A: the small cross is blown up into a huge, blurry blue block that competes with the headline. The dates row is jammed against the headline column and the illustration ends in a hard-edged box. B keeps the cross small, but the layout is scattered: the cross sits right against 'LIVONIA', 'WORSHIP & BIBLE STUDY' floats alone between the copy and the image, the headline is centred while the copy below it isn't, and the dates are tiny and stuck in the lower-left corner. Both are flawed, but A's distorted cross is the worse failure.

A puts the red 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow below the headline and left-aligned against a centered headline, which breaks both reading order and alignment. Its brown owl is blown up into a centered focal point that competes with the headline, the blue owl is shrunk to a tiny afterthought jammed into the bottom-left corner, and the confetti is clipped into a band with a large empty area beneath. B keeps the original structure: hanging owl at the top, eyebrow above a dominant centered headline, blue owl anchoring the bottom. Its flaws are confetti stars sitting on and around the headline letters, and the confetti field visibly cut off as a strip at its top edge.

A is just the original shrunk into a narrow strip in the centre of the banner, with roughly 85% of the canvas left as dead white space. Its 'LOVE. CARE. KIDS.' headline is tiny and the thin yellow frame is barely visible, so it fails fit-to-format and readability. B at least rearranges the design left to right with a readable headline block and a larger photo, but it is broken too: an empty outlined frame sits alone in the middle, a stray clipped yellow bar sits at the top-right edge, and the headline, frame and photo float as unrelated fragments separated by large gaps.

A and B look the same: each scales the original's centred wordmark and two mirrored illustration clusters down to 320x50. The 'CREATIVE AGENCY' line ends up about 7 px tall and hard to read. The illustration clusters are cropped and crowd the canvas edges, and the figures are too small to make out. Neither candidate rearranges anything, so both are faithful but cramped scale-downs, and I can't see a meaningful difference between them.

A: the headline is bigger and reads clearly as the focal point. But the photo is cropped so tightly that the couple is barely recognisable, the URL is tiny, and the heart shape has shrunk to a faint stray outline next to it. B: the photo shows the couple better and the URL is easier to read, but the headline is smaller and weaker, and the heart shape sits under the text as a near-invisible broken fragment that looks like a mistake. Neither keeps the heart-shaped panel holding the copy, which defined the original.

A: the symptom list is tiny and run together into paragraph-like lines ('Shortness of breath Dry cough', 'Sore throat Headache' on one line), so it no longer reads as a list. The hashtag is shrunk into an inset chip, the CTA is near-illegible fine print, and there are dead gaps above and below the doctor. B: the list keeps its stacked structure at a readable size, and the headline → illustration → list → CTA order works for a skyscraper. But the yellow hashtag bar is cut off at half width and jammed into the corner, the list is crammed against the CTA, and the CTA sits too close to the bottom edge.

A pulls the T's crossbar in from the right edge and stops the stem at about 80% height. That loses the original's bleed and leaves a dead blue band across the bottom third, and the headline block is undersized for the square, so the canvas feels half-empty. B keeps the crossbar bleeding off the right edge, as in the original, and sets larger, more legible type. Its flaws are a stem that still floats short of the bottom edge instead of bleeding, and an empty lower-left quadrant that makes the composition top-heavy.

A shrinks the five-line headline to tiny, barely legible type, leaves it floating at an arbitrary x≈170 with dead blue on the left, and moves the red T to the right as an unrelated block, so the original's layering of the headline across the T's bar is gone. B is less bad because its text is larger and anchored to the left margin, but it still stacks five cramped lines that touch the top and bottom edges instead of reflowing into a single line for the banner, leaves a large empty middle, and keeps the T as a disconnected shape on the far right.

A: the headline is still stacked in five short lines inside a wide banner, so it ends up as tiny text in the left corner. The red T is cut off from the copy and pushed far right, with a large dead gap between them. The text-over-T layering that defined the original is gone. B: same five-line stack, but the text is even smaller and harder to read. The T and the text sit together in the middle, leaving the left edge and the whole right third empty, so the layout looks lopsided. A wins narrowly on readability and a natural left-to-right reading order.

A gets the hierarchy wrong. The secondary teal line 'Great location and modern equipment!' is set larger than the headline and sits jammed against the top-left edge. The 'Traditional Ceramics Workshop' headline is shrunk to a small centred line, and the contact copy on the right is tiny and crowds the edge. B correctly makes the orange headline the dominant element on the left. However, its right-hand column crams the body copy, teal line, dashes, phone and URL into microscopic, near-illegible text that is jammed against the right edge.

A shrinks the crowd illustration into a small strip in the top-left, leaving dead white space beside it and losing the key image. Its quote breaks badly, with an orphaned 'OF THOUGHTFUL' line and a ragged 'THE WORLD; INDEED,', and the attribution needlessly wraps onto two lines. B keeps the crowd large and full-width across the top, so it stays faithful to the original. It shares the same awkward forced breaks ('OF THOUGHTFUL' orphan), and its text block and one-line attribution sit cramped against the left, right and bottom edges with almost no margin.

Both break the original idea: the quote is pulled out of the floral frame, and stock placeholder text ('BEAUTY / ILLUSTRATION / HAND DRAWN ELEMENTS') now shows inside the empty frame. That is a serious fidelity error in each. A is weaker still: the attribution sits right under 'MAKEUP.' with almost no gap, the quote is small for the canvas, and both halves float in a lot of dead white space. B sets a larger, more confident quote with a proper gap above 'CAROLYN MURPHY' and fills the banner more evenly, though the illustration is still shrunk and the frame is empty.

A breaks the diamond-mosaic photo apart: the city image is a small loose rectangle, the white diamond lattice floats empty beside it, the divider line is stranded in the middle, and the brown diamonds are cut off at the left edge, so the signature graphic is gone. Its body copy is also tiny. B keeps the mosaic, the diamonds and the type intact, but it is a shrunk copy with large empty bands above (about 100px) and below (about 120px). The headline and body text are small for a tall format, and the vertical URL is nearly illegible.

A moves the headline and copy into a cramped block at the top, demotes the iconic shape row (the original's hero) to a small strip mid-canvas with dead space above and below, and strands the 3-day-event body text at the bottom, below the URL it points to ('follow the link:' ends with nothing after it). B keeps the original order (shapes at top, then headline, then pink subhead) and stays faithful. Its flaws: the blocks are spread out with large, roughly equal gaps, so they read as loose fragments; the URL still comes before 'follow the link:'; the body text is tiny with tight spacing ('IN NY' reads as 'INNY').

A is unusable: the headline is white text on a white canvas, so it is invisible apart from stray fragments. The forest image is a small central strip, and the subhead and body copy are cut off at its edge. B is just the original shrunk into the middle of the banner. It leaves huge white dead zones on both sides, the body copy is illegibly tiny, and nothing has been rearranged for the wide format. Still, B is intact and on brand, so it is the less bad of the two.

A keeps the stripe-and-card composition intact, but the red stripe no longer bleeds off the right edge and leaves a thin white sliver there; it is mostly a shifted copy rather than a real rearrangement, with a large empty white left third. B breaks the background: the stripes are narrowed with a white gap between blue and red, they stop short of the bottom and leave a dead white band, and a stray hairline sits at the left. The background no longer reads as the original's continuous bands.

A keeps the original structure: the cat group is large and anchored to the bottom edge, with the headline above it. But the headline has shrunk to a small two-line block that no longer spans the width, so it loses its poster-like punch. B makes the headline larger, but shrinks the key cat illustration to a tiny cluster floating at the bottom, leaving a big dead purple band between them. The imagery becomes trivial and the design no longer feels the same.

A keeps the headline-over-tagline hierarchy and a clean text block, but both framing rules are gone from the text: one has landed as a stray black line across the cup and box in the photo, and the bottom rule is missing, so the bracket motif is broken and there's an obvious artifact. B flips the hierarchy: 'Order online' shrinks to small text while 'food & drinks' becomes the largest element and runs over the takeout box ('drinks' collides with busy imagery). The two rules also float far above and below the tiny headline, leaving a lot of empty space.

A is just the original portrait layout dropped into the middle of the square, with large empty white strips left and right. The yellow dash accents have come loose and float to the left of the photo, and the top yellow bar sits off-centre against the right edge, so it reads as an unadapted copy. Its one strength is that the headline still sits over the photo the way the original does. B does rearrange the design, but the thin yellow frame on the left is mostly empty: the headline box is pushed into its top third with dead white space below, and nothing links it to the photo beside it. The dash accents are scattered over the photo, the top yellow bar is stranded at the top, and the photo is cut off from the brand frame, so the original's layered look is lost.

A: the headline is blown up so far that 'the limit' runs about 90 px into the busy striped building photo, and 'us.' sits tight against the right edge. In both, the photo is a short letterboxed strip with empty white bands above and below, so the layout looks like the original pasted onto a taller canvas rather than rearranged for it. B: same letterboxed photo and dead space, but the headline stays close to its original size and only 'the' clips the tip of the image, so the collision is much smaller and the margins hold.

A is a broken layout. The headline, URL and brand name are missing entirely. The blue panel is an empty slanted shape. The white device-outline logo sits on the white background, where it is nearly invisible. The phone photo is cut down to a tiny strip, and the elements are scattered with huge dead areas around them. B is just the original banner shrunk into a thin strip in the middle of the tall canvas, so the headline and URL are far too small to read and roughly 90% of the canvas is empty white. It keeps the design's colours and arrangement, but it was not reworked at all for the vertical format. B is less bad only because the brand and message still survive, even though they can't be read at this size.

A keeps the original lockup intact and at strong scale (& + Baby/Toddler + BEDDING read as one unit), but it just shifts the 90px strip into the middle of the taller canvas. That leaves large dead navy bands above and below, and BEDDING's final G sits jammed against the right dot column. B has the same dead bands and also shrinks the &/Baby Toddler lockup and BEDDING. It then splits them with a wide gap, so BEDDING floats as a separate, weaker element and the headline loses prominence and grouping.

A just shrinks the leaderboard into a thin strip across the middle of the portrait canvas, with roughly 80% dead blue above and below. 'DENTAL SERVICES' is tiny and the decorative teeth are cut flat along the strip's bottom edge, so it is a squashed copy, not a resize. B does rearrange the layout, but the headline is a small single line in the top-left that is dwarfed by the huge tooth-and-woman illustration. The illustration is sliced flat at its bottom edge and floats in the middle of the canvas, and the tiny row of teeth sits in the bottom-left corner as a separate fragment, leaving uneven empty bands. Weak hierarchy and balance, but still far better than A.

A rearranges for the 320x50 strip: 'DENTAL SERVICES' sits on one line, big and readable, and the woman and tooth stay on the right. But the small teeth on the left are bunched into a messy cluster against the edge, the headline nearly touches the graphics on both sides, and most of the airy tooth pattern from the original is gone. B is just the original shrunk: the two-line headline is tiny and hard to read at this size, the woman figure is very small, and the wide white tooth shapes take up more room than the message. It keeps the original look but fails readability and hierarchy.

A keeps the original's T. Its bar runs off the right edge and the stem drops close to the bottom, but the stem stops about 65px short of the edge instead of bleeding off. The bottom-left also turns into a large empty block, and 'NOW!' crowds the edge of the bar. B's T floats inside the canvas: the bar stops short of the right edge and the stem ends about 150px above the bottom. That leaves a dead blue band along the bottom and a smaller headline in the top-left corner, which reads as a shrunken copy rather than a deliberate layout.

A just shrinks the whole portrait poster into a narrow strip in the middle of the wide banner. That leaves huge empty white areas on both sides, and the body copy and the March 21 date become too small to read; it is a letterbox, not a resize. B is unusable: the headline and the date are white or cream on the white canvas, so they are invisible or half-invisible, and the copy and the 'Joint celebration' line are cut off at the edges of the narrow forest panel. The divider rules also float loose at the bottom.

A inverts the hierarchy: the headline 'Order online' is shrunk to a small label while 'food & drinks' becomes the largest text and runs over the takeout box image. The two rules float apart from the type, so the lockup is broken. B keeps the headline/subhead lockup intact and readable, but the bottom rule is gone and the top rule has been flung onto the cup and box photo as a stray line, which is an unwanted collision. Its text block also sits off-centre in the left panel.

A: the image strip is not extended into the taller canvas, so empty white bands sit above and below it, and the 't' of 'the' just touches the tip of the building image (in the original the headline stays clear of it). B has the same empty top and bottom bands, and its larger headline pushes 'the limit' well into the striped building photo, so the text sits on a busy image. That collision is worse than A's slight touch.
